title: Managed DISABLED Claude row: its not-run updateDetail must not tell the user to enable it (ruling 28 follow-up)
description: Found by the adversarial review of LCLI-604 (opum-ai/lore-cli#305), finding S1. When the deciding Claude row has scope managed and state disabled, lore agents --target claude --force reports update not-run with the ordinary disabled detail: "lore agents never enables a disabled plugin; enable it with the remedy, then update". Next to the agreed managed remedy ("...which only an administrator can change"), that tells the user to do something only an administrator can do, and promises an update that ruling 28 says never happens. A bare lore agents --force on the same row also says "lore agents --target claude --force updates this one", which is false. Only the list runs in both cases, so the wording is wrong but no wrong action is taken. Proposed fix: use the agreed managed updateDetail ("the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated") for installed AND disabled managed rows. That widens the scope of a ruling-(d) string, so it needs quest-cli to agree for parity (proposed to quest-cli 2026-09-26, no answer when this was filed); implement only once it is agreed, or once opum-agent rules.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest-cli has agreed (or opum-agent has ruled) which updateDetail a managed disabled row carries, recorded here with the agreement

A managed disabled row under --target claude --force and under a bare --force carries that detail, and no detail on a managed row mentions enabling or a runnable update, proven through a stub port that logs every call
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: AC1 RULING, opum-agent 2026-09-26T21:25Z (successor orchestrator, cross-session message): a managed deciding row carries the agreed managed updateDetail "the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated" whether it is installed OR disabled. No detail on a managed row may mention enabling, or an update the user can run. This is ruling 28 applied (opum-doc main: "A managed deciding row is never updated ... the remedy names the administrator own managed settings, not a command the plugin user can run"), not a new ruling, so no ADR amendment is needed. The same ruling was sent to quest-cli for parity under QCLI-381.

Implemented: notRunDetail (src/core/agent-plugins.ts) returns MANAGED_SCOPE_UPDATE_DETAIL for a managed deciding row that is installed OR disabled, ahead of the bare-call and ordinary disabled details. Tests (test/agent-plugins.test.ts): "--target claude --force on managed DISABLED ... never enable (LCLI-608)", "a bare lore agents --force: managed installed AND disabled ... (LCLI-608)", and the fake-claude subprocess test "ruling 28 (LCLI-604) ... starts the list command only", which now pins the detail for both states. All go through a port or a fake claude that logs every call (only "claude plugin list --json" runs), and they assert no managed updateDetail mentions enable, --force, --target or "claude plugin". Mutation: reverting the source change turns exactly those 3 red. Docs: cli-surface (both passages) and the lore instructions agents topic. Gates: bun test 3661 pass / 0 fail, bun run lore check 0 errors, typecheck clean.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#308 (CI pull_request run 36273163241 on faed4c0e, plus the closing commit). A managed deciding Claude row, installed or disabled, reports update not-run with the agreed managed updateDetail "the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated", and no managed detail mentions enabling or a runnable update (ruling 28 applied, opum-agent 2026-09-26T21:25Z). Proven through a logging port and a fake claude, where only the list runs. Reverting the source change turns exactly 3 tests red. Docs updated in cli-surface and lore instructions agents. quest-cli receives the same ruling under QCLI-381.
